transcript: The image depicts a juxtaposition between a newly constructed skyscraper and a relatively older building in the foreground. The skyscraper, towering approximately 50 stories high, stands prominently against the skyline. Its facade, predominantly glass, reflects some of the surrounding older buildings. Contrastingly, the older building, estimated to be around ten stories tall, exhibits a more intricate design, likely constructed with materials such as brick, wood, and tiles. This stark contrast in architectural styles between the two buildings is evident, highlighting the evolution of urban landscapes over time.

The graph shows the output of processor chips over a week, with figures provided for each day. The greatest number of chips was produced on Friday, with about 16,000 chips produced. A similar number was produced on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday with just under 14,000 chips each day.

About 10,000 chips were produced on Monday, while 7,000 were produced on Saturday. There were no chips produced on Sunday.

The image shows a school timetable for Monday in Semester 1.

Lectures start at 9 a.m. and conclude at 4 p.m. The first lecture is Introductory Statistics at 9 a.m. The next lecture is at 10 a.m. with Psychology. Lunch is at 12 noon. There is an English Literature tutorial which lasts from 1 to 3 p.m. The last lecture is Economics, which starts at 3 p.m. and concludes at 4 p.m.

This diagram shows how a selection of 100 second-year university students traveled to university.

60 students said that they traveled by train, 30 stated that they traveled by car, while 10 students stated that they traveled by both car and train.

One could conclude that most respondents traveled to university by train, a minority traveled only by car, while a small number of the respondents, 10%, traveled by both train and car.

The organisational chart shows the hierarchy of members of Management team. As a director, Jim Tognol is ranked first. Right below him is Chris Gale who is his assistant. Below Chris Gale are three other managers. First one is Michalle Davis the marketing manager, next is Adrian Moranis the business development manager and lastly Marjorie Smith the customer ralations manager.

This is a simplified map of part of a university campus.

It shows the locations of the Thomas Mann Library, the Science Labs, the Undergraduate Lecture Theaters and the Sports Field.

The largest building is the lecture theaters. The Thomas Mann Library is a long narrow building. The Science Labs are near both the library and the lecture theaters. The Sports Field is near the library and the lecture theaters.

The countries with the highest rates of boat travel were Nauru, the Federated States of Micronesia, the Cook Islands, Tonga and Niue.

The rates of boat travel for these five countries ranged from 94.5% to 81.7%.

Nauru had the Highest rate of boat travel by residents at 94.5%.

The world's most populous region, with approximately 35 million residents, is Tokyo.

The ten largest urban areas in the world range from approximately 12 million to 35 million.

Tokyo, Mexico City and New York are the three most populous regions in the world.

The presented table illustrates the rankings of global cities with the highest cost of living for the years 2007 and 2008 across five cities. Notably, in both 2007 and 2008, Moscow consistently held the top position as the city with the highest cost of living. Alongside Moscow, Tokyo, London, Oslo, and Seoul emerged as the top five most expensive cities to reside in globally. Throughout the transition from 2007 to 2008, Moscow maintained its position as the world's most expensive city. During this period, Tokyo and Oslo exhibited an increase in their relative costliness, while London and Seoul experienced a decrease in relative costliness.

On December 20, 2008, the Australian Share market opened at 3620. It closed the day at 3560. Relative to the previous day, Australian share prices opened slightly higher by 30 points, then gradually eased to close lower by 30 points. Between 10 and 11 a.m. the Australian share market lost 40 points, it stabilized for several hours before falling further between 3 and 4 p.m.

There is a relationship between how tired a subject is and response time.

The highly fatigued subjects have a much slower response rate of over 3.5 seconds, compared to alert subjects who have a response time of about 0.8 seconds.
The sun is mainly made up of hydrogen and helium, with very small amounts of oxygen, carbon, nitrogen and silicon. There are about three-quarters of hydrogen, and one quarter of helium.

The reported population densities range from just above zero persons per square kilometer to about 18,000 people in Singapore.

The most densely populated country reported was Singapore. Bermuda and Bangladesh had moderate population densities, while the densities of Australia and Greenland were very low.

Azerbaijan is a country situated in the Middle East, between Asia and Europe.

Its territory is divided into two discrete areas. To the east it is bordered by water, and to the north by the Russian Federation and Georgia, Armenia to the west and Iran to the south. It has an irregularly shaped border.

The graph shows the performance of Australia among 194 nations in the world.

It ranks 19th in terms of GNP per person at 32,220 US dollars.

Life expectancy for Australians is 80 years, ranking 6th in the world.

Its literacy rate is the highest in the world with 99% of the population able to read and write.

It ranks 20th on the measure of infant mortality with 5 deaths per 1000 live births. Australia is rated 3rd on the Human Development Index.

The graph provides information about Brazil's climate.

Brazil's temperatures range from an average high temperature of 30 degrees Celsius or 86 degrees Fahrenheit during its summer months of December, January and February to a low of just under 20 degrees Celsius or 68 degrees Fahrenheit in July.

Brazil is rainiest during the summer months peaking at around 15 centimeters or six inches of rain in February. It is noticeably less rainy during the winter months with monthly rainfall of just 5 centimeters or two inches in late July.

The graph provides information about consumption and spending in China.

There are 13 cars and 241 phones per thousand people in China.

China's annual spending on Defense is 1.9% of GDP. Education is 2.2% of GDP while expenditure on health amounts to 2% of GDP.

The graph shows the main source of tourists into Ecuador.

Most people visiting Ecuador as tourists come from Colombia, with 27% of all visitors coming from that country. This is followed by the United States with 21% of total arrivals and Peru with 20%. The remaining 32% of tourists come from a number of other countries, not specified in the graph.

The Finnish Parliament is made up of 200 seats. The Center Party, KESK, has 26% of the seats, followed closely by the National Coalition Party of KOK with 25%.

The Social Democratic Panty or SDP won 23% of the votes, followed by LeftAlliance with 9%, the Green League with 7%, and the Swedish People's Party with 4%. A collection of other candidates won 6% of the votes.

New Zealand's main export markets are Australia, the USA, Japan, China and the UK. Exports to Australia account for 21% of all exports from New Zealand. The USA accounts for 14%, Japan 11%, China 6%, followed by the UK at 5%. The information also indicates that another 43% of total exports go to a range of other destinations.

The graph shows population trends in Europe and Asia as a percentage of world population between 1750 and 2000.

Asia had a much bigger percentage of the world's population during this period than Europe. Asia's proportion dropped from 65 to 55 percent between 1750 and 1950 but reached 60 percent in 2000.

Europe's population was fairly stable from 1750 to 1850 at just over 20 percent of world population. Then it rose slightly in 1900 before falling by more than half to just over 10 percent in 2000.

The charts show why males and females stopped going to school.

In both cases the main reason was that they had completed their studies. This applies to 65 percent of females and 60 percent of males. The second reason was that they had got a job, but 25 percent of males had work compared with 12 percent of females.

Almost the same percentage of females also left school for personal or family reasons while only 4 percent of males did.

A very small percentage of students left due to illness. 3 percent of males and 5 percent of females and a slightly bigger percentage left for other non-specified reasons.

The chart shows the future trends in the percentage of American citizens over 65 years old.

In 2010, about 13 percent of US citizens were over 65. This figure is predicted to rise steadily so that by 2035 it will be 20 percent.

Between 2010 and 2030 the rise will be quite steady, whereas between 2030 and 2035 the rise is less significant, suggesting that the increase in the aging population may peek shortly after 2035.

However, the rise will have serious implications in areas such as the provision of government services.

The graph shows revenue growth in millions of dollars for 2 companies between 2006 and 2024.

The revenue of company X is forecast to rise steadily from $300 million to $1,800 million in 2024. Company Y's revenue started at 0 in 2006 and is likely to increase slowly to about $400 million in 2019.

After that, however, predictions are that the company's growth will surge between 2019 and 2024 to just overtake company X at $1,900 million.

The graph shows reading achievement over 3 years for 2 groups of students, successful readers and struggling readers, measured in words per minute.

Successful readers make faster overall progress than struggling readers. Over 3 years, they go quite steadily from 20 words per minute to 120 words per minute. Struggling readers make smaller gains and seem to regress a little in the fall perhaps because they don't read much during the summer break.

Overall, they go from about 8 words per minute to about 50 in the same period of time.

The diagram shows a shadouf which is a method of collecting water.

It consists of a raised walkway that is attached to a post by a pivot to form a lever. At the end of the lever there is a rope and a bucket. The operator climbs up to the walkway and uses his way to balance the lever. He moves forward so that the lever falls and the bucket tips into the water and then he walks backward again so that his weight raises the lever and the bucket of water rises for collection.

The plan shows the layout of a student apartment.

There is one large living area with a table and chairs and an arm chair with a small kitchen and small bathroom to one side. There is a separate bedroom with a bed and wardrobe and two windows.

The study area is on the right of the entrance and is part of the living area. It has a desk near the window and would probably also have book shelves.

The apartment seems quite convenient for a student living on their own.

The bar graph depicts the total numbers of urban population in each country and the line graph shows the percentage of the population that is urban.

From the 21 countries mentioned in the graph, 10 have over half of their populations residing in urban areas. Nauru has its 100% population in the urban area while Tokelau and Wallis and Futuna residents live in rural areas.

Overall, we can see a rapid growth of urbanization in Pacific Island countries and territories.

The graph shows the earning distribution in Utopia by gender with respect to the number of people.

From the given data, it is clear that there are the most number of men and women earning between 35k-39k $. There is also a healthy number of people who are earning in the lowest income group of 0-4k $ indicating unemployment and low-income rate.

As the income of both men and women starts increasing from 40k to 85+k $, the number of people starts decreasing gradually. There are only handful of people who makes to the highest income group of $85000+.

The image shows the number related to migration to and from the UK.

The notable data is the year 1992 Which recorded a negative migration. The number of immigrants moving to the UK has been constant since 2004. But the number of people leaving the country has dropped off significantly in the past couple of years hence there is an increase in net migration.

The image shows the distribution of population among the continents projected by United Nations from 2015 to 2100.

A major growth is projected to be in Africa, approximately 270 percent while Europe is expected to decline in population. The continent which foresees 2nd major growth is Asia.

To conclude, it is quite clear that more than 99% of world growth from 2015 to 2100 is expected to be among the lower income nations.

The pie chart illustrates the overall market share of US Ebook unit sales held by each retailer.

From the given data, I analyze that 98% of all consumer ebook purchases happen through just five major ebook retailers. Among those five, Amazon constitutes major chunk With 74% followed by Apple iBooks With 12%, B&N Nook 8%, and Kobo US 3%. The surprising figure is of internet giant, Google Play With 2%.

The image describes ocean circulation conveyor belt.

From the illustration, it is quite clear that the ocean water near the equator has a high salt content. The water loses its heat when it reaches the poles and as the cold water reaches near the equator, it heats up and rises to the surface.

Overall, the ocean water causes heat transfer.

The chart compares total population growth of Canada in the factor of natural and migratory increase.

The data illustrates migration as the factor of population growth. The period between 1978-1988 is characterized by the higher natural increase. The late 1990s seems a period of transition when natural growth began falling.

To conclude, migratory increase plays an important role in population growth after the 1990s.

The picture is about out of sight, out of mind, which thoroughly describes the continent-sized vortex of plastic waste blighting the pacific.

From the picture, we can see that the Eastern Patch is located to the south of Russia and east of Japan.

The Western Patch lies off the west coast of Canada, Mexico and the United States, very close to Hawaii.

The translucent soup of the degrading plastic waste has already accumulated to a depth of 10 meters garbage patch.

Furthermore, the rotation pattern created by the north pacific gyre current is streaming clockwise and counterclockwise around the two garbage patches.  In summary, plastic that has been dumped into the sea is causing a severe damage to the marine-ecosystem.

This picture shows the national flags of the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.

The most obvious characteristic is that these flags share the same colors, which are red, green, white and black.

Also, their shapes look similar. On the left side, there is a red rectangle on Arab's flag, while there is a red chevron with a white star on Jordan's flag.

Finally, on the right side, although the white rectangle is in the middle on both flags, on Arab's flag, the green shape is on the top, while on Jordan's flag, it is at the bottom. This is also true for the black color. In conclusion, there are similarities between these two flags.

The bar graph grouped workers by education level.

It is obvious that those with more education have higher earnings and lower rates of unemployment than those with less education. Professional degree holders get average weekly earnings of $1,730 and have the lowest unemployment rate of 1.5%.

To summarize, the earning increases and unemployment decrease as educational attainment rises.

The given bar graph compares the fertility rates of women in 6 different Gulf countries between 1990 and 2000.

Oman has the highest rate among all other Gulf countries in both the period.

By contrast, women of Bahrain has the lowest fertility rate.

From the data, it is evident that fertility rate in Gulf countries has decreased from 1990 to 2000.

The diagram shows the process of producing electricity in a home using solar panels.

There are 6 distinct steps in this process, beginning with the capture of energy from sunlight. A charge controller regulates the flow of PV electricity into the batteries. This current is passed to a battery system, which changes it to DC current or/and to an inverter, which changes it to AC current.

To sum up, it describes how domestic electricity is produced using solar power.

The given pie charts compare the percentage of customer service response in the years 2005 and 2010.

In 2005, only 5% of the people considered the customer service to be excellent, while 14% rated it as good. In 2010, these numbers increased dramatically to 28% and 39%.

Overall, the trend suggests that there was a significant improvement in customer services in 2010 compared to 2005.

The graph compares the GDP per capita of India and UK from 1700 to 1950.

The GDP has been adjusted for inflation. It is interesting to note that while India's GDP remained constant from 1700 to 1950 at around $500, the GDP of UK increased steadily from the time of East India Company starting in 1750 and sharply after 1850 when the British Raj was established.

By 1950 UK's GDP was around 14 times that of India. At the same time, the population ratio of UK and India changed from almost 1:20 in the 1700s to almost 1:7 in 1950.

The line graph shows the information about Radio and Television audiences in the UK in October to December 1992 measured in percentage.

At 1.00 am, more than 5% people started to watch TV which increased to approximately 15% at 13.00pm and further increased to 45% at 21.00pm then drop to 15% at night 23.00. On the other hand, 25% of people liked to listen to Radio at 8.00 in the morning whereas this trend declined to approximately 5% at night 23.00.

To conclude, it can be said that watching TV and listening radio both were irreversibly proportionate to each other.

The line graph shows the number of visitors per month in summer measured in thousands to watch different Museums in 2013 from June to September. 

In June, the highest visitors were found in British Museum which increased to more than 700. In July then declined in the month of September followed by the number of visitors were recorded in Natural History Museum that ranging between 400 to 600 for a given period. On the other hand, 400 visitors went to Science Museum in June which decline to its least value that was 300 in August and reached to its highest value in September. To conclude, British Museum was famous among others.

The picture shows a major city that seems to be densely populated.

There are several tall skyscrapers in the background while there are a number of smaller buildings in the front.

It seems that the smaller buildings were built much earlier than the ones in the background. They all look like some kind of office buildings. This is probably the central business district of the city. But if you look further behind the buildings you will see a tall white mountain that seems to have had snow recently.

The pie chart shows the top exports from India in the year 2013-2014.

The exports were measured in US dollars. The first thing that is clear from the chart is that petro products accounted for the biggest share of the exports at 20%. The next highest contributor to Indian exports was Gems and Jewellery at 13%.

Agriculture sector which exports things like rice made up 10% of the total exports.

Fabric & textiles and Transport Parts each provided 7% while Machine and Pharma provided 5% each.

Metal Products and Electronics made 3% and Plastics were at 2% of the export.

All remaining exports provided the remaining 25%.

The table compares the output of waste produced by six different countries in 1980, 1990 and 2000 in million tons.

In 1980, US produced 131 million tons of waste material while the figures for Japan stood at 28 million tons.

By 2000, in US production of waste had risen to 192 million tons while Japan figure had risen to 53 million tons. The lowest amount of waste was produced by Ireland and Portugal.

In conclusion, the figures for almost all of the countries contributing to the output of waste material had risen over the 20 year period.

The bar chart compares how many Olympic medals won by twelve countries in the world.

The USA tops the chart with the highest number of Gold, Silver and Bronze medals with about two thousand three hundred total medals. It is followed by the Soviet Union with one thousand medals.

The UK and France managed to make around seven hundred and six hundred medals respectively. The lowest number of medals were won by Japan and China with less than four hundred medals.

In conclusion, investment in professional sports is probably the reason for impressive achievement by the united states in the Olympics.

The line graph compares the three companies in terms of their waste output between the years 2000 and 2015.

In 2000, company A produced 12 tons of waste while companies B and C produced just around 8 tons and 4 tons of waste material respectively. Over the following five years, the waste outputs of company B and C rose by around 2 tons but the figure for company A fell by approximately one ton.

In conclusion, the amount of waste produced by company C increased considerably.

This pie chart represents the car ownership statistics in Canada.

The majority of the population possesses at least one car.

One-quarter of the total population of two cars while a very small number of car owners stated that they have three or more cars.

About twenty percent of the population does not possess any four wheelers.

In conclusion, about eighty percent of the population was managed to have a car still a significant number of people are without a proper family vehicle.

This horizontal bar graph depicts various shopping methods which are affecting the satisfaction of consumers.

The survey was done with a customer base of 500. The vertical axis displays the various shopping methods such as local shop, internet, supermarket and private shopping used by consumers.

The results show that the percentage of neutral consumers is almost same across all methods. However, consumers are more satisfied when using private shopping methods and local shops.

The following line chart gives information on median pre-tax income by age and gender in the UK. We can see three lines, in which the blue one represents male, the green one female, and the red one both. It is clear from the graph that the average income for females is lower than in males.  The figure for males rises from 12,000 at under 20, reaches the highest point of 30,000 at the age of 45 to 49, then falls to the lowest point of about 18,000 at 70 to 74. In the same way, the figure for females rises from 11,000 to the highest point of 21,000 at about 30 to 34, and falls to the lowest point of 15 thousand at 75 and over.

The following image gives information regarding the formation of icebergs. Firstly, it starts with snow, falling from the sky and turning into an ice sheet on the bedrock. After that, the ice sheet stretches beyond the grounding line into the ocean to form an ice shelf. Finally, under the ice shelf, the warm ocean water melts the ice until it breaks into icebergs. This graph describes the whole process of iceberg formation.

The following image represents a map of South America and gives information about the rainforest distribution.  According to this graph, the tropical rainforest, in light green, extends over multiple countries such as Brazil, Bolivia, Peru, Colombia, Suriname. We can also see a narrow, long stretch of tropical rain forest lying along the eastern coast of South America, next to the Atlantic Ocean. Another type of rainforest, the temperate rainforest, can be found in the southern part of the continent. It is coloured in dark green on the map and exclusively lies over Chile.

The following graph gives information about the water cycle in nature.  The water evaporates from oceans and ground to form clouds in the sky. This step is called evaporation. After that, the transportation step, means that clouds are moving inland and near the mountains. This starts the next step which is precipitation. The water runoff on the surface to form rivers and end back into oceans.

This picture gives information about the process of germination. In the first step, a seed is buried in the soil and it develops a green embryo. In the second step, the seed coat begins to peel off and black roots begin to grow. After that, a light green cotyledon starts to emerge from the ground. Then, some dark green foliage leaves grow before the plant is fully grown.

The following picture gives information about the heights of different types of penguins. According to this graph, the emperor is the tallest of all with about 1.2 meters in height. After that, the second tallest is king penguin, which is about 1 meter tall. All other penguins which are Gentoo, Chinstrap, Macaroni and Adelie, are very similar in height, between 60 and 80 centimeters tall. In conclusion, this graph compares the heights of several kinds of penguins.

The following graph gives information about journeys made in the UK in 2006 according to their purpose. The items include walking, education, shopping, personal business, school run, day trip, sport, entertainment, and commuting. According to this graph, the highest value for women is shopping, with about 23%. On the other side, the highest value for men is commuting and business, which is 23%. The lowest figure is the same for both men and women for holiday and day trips, which is around 3%.

The following bar chart gives information about the number of texts sent on a typical day between adults versus teens. According to the graph, 51% of adults send on average 1 to 10 texts a day. This figure drops to only 13% for 11 t0 20 texts and keeps on decreasing as the number of texts increase. On the other side, the highest figure for teens is 29% for 101+ texts sent on a typical day.

The image shows information about an auditorium. According to the image the seating arrangement is well designed so that every member of the audience should be able to see clearly at all times with an unobstructed sightline, the lecturer stage is in the middle of the lecture hall, equipped with a whiteboard and a podium. I can see from this picture that the indoor lighting is very bright and there are six windows in the walls.

This line graph contains the information about the population of Litchfield from 1901 to 2011. The information is shown in a line and the population is shown by the blue-shaded area under the line. It starts at about 7,500 in 1901 and gradually increased to about 10,000 in 1951. After that, there is a sharp increase in the population and reached about 23,000 in 1971. The increase slowed down later and concluded at about 32,000 in 2011. There was a slight decrease from 1991 to 2001. In conclusion, the graph provides useful information about the population of Litchfield.

The pie chart represents the approximate composition of the air. As we can see from the chart there are oxygen, other gases, and nitrogen in the atmosphere. In addition, Nitrogen is the first most abundant gas in the atmosphere which occupies 79%, flowing by Oxygen which is 20%. In terms of other gases, it includes carbon dioxide, argon, and water vapor have a proportion of 1%. In conclusion, the chart is very useful since it clearly shows the composition of the air.

The picture gives information about London's expected energy target by 2030 for different sectors such as heating and cooling, transport and power. Heating and cooling represent 51% of the total energy consumption of London. This figure only includes 10% of renewable energy. In addition, there is 32% of total energy consumption used for transport, which only covers 3% of renewable energy. Lastly, 17% of energy is used by power, while it produces 26% of renewable energy. In conclusion, the major sector for renewable energy is power.

The bar chart shows information about Internet users who accessed via a mobile phone in Great Britain in 2011 based on different age groups. As we can see from the chart, the youngest age group constitutes the highest proportion of mobile users which represents about 70%. This figure steadily decreases as the age increases. It reaches the lowest point of just under 10% of the 65+ age group. In conclusion, the main users who accessed the Internet via a mobile phone are the age group of 16 to 24 years.

The picture gives information about how a ship lock works and how the process is done. As we can see from the picture, a boat enters the lock, which is a big chamber in the water with moveable gates A and B at each end. Once the boat is inside the lock, door A closes and mechanism D opens to release the water from the lock downstream. Once the water is level, door B opens to release the ship. In conclusion, a lock enables a boat to easily navigate a river that is not level.

The following graph gives information about different age groups by gender. The items include females and males. The data shows that the percentage decreases as the age increases. Females represent 15.5% of the 1 to 15 age group. This figure gradually decreases to reach the minimum value of 0.4% for the 85+ age group. This pattern is very similar for males with a minimum of 0.8% for the oldest age group. In conclusion, females and males have the almost same percentage in any age group.

The diagrams illustrate the modification of building a ground floor from an existing plan. It is noticeable that one of the internal walls and storage was removed to make the hall to be a part of the living room while both entrance doors remain unchanged.

In the new plan, two internal doors were relocated from two sides of the hall to one end of the internal wall where both internal doors are next to each other. At the same time, the position of the stairs in the old plan was moved to one corner of the living room. By doing so, more space can be seen in the living room in the proposed plan and make it easier for people to access the kitchen from the living room.

Furthermore, one more change can be noticed in the kitchen. In the old plan, there was no kitchen furniture while it has been added to the new plan.

The following graph gives information about different types of E-waste. The graph differentiates electronic and electric waste. Both types represent 50% of the total E-waste. Electric waste is composed of 20% of refrigerators and 30% of washing machines and dryers. On the other side, the value of computers, telephones, fax and printers is around fifteen percent, which is similar to DVD and other players. Televisions and monitors represent 10% of the total waste. In conclusion, this graph gives useful information.

The following graph gives information about the mosquito life cycle. It shows how the process is done. The items include adult, eggs, larva and pupa. You can see from this graph that the first step is the adult laying eggs on the surface of the water. After that, the eggs hatch in water and a mosquito larva emerges. The larva lives in the water and develops into the third stage of the life cycle called, a pupa. The pupa also lives in the water. Finally, the mosquito emerges from the pupal case onto the water's surface and flies away, ready to begin its lifecycle.

The following picture gives information about the minimum ice thickness guidelines for new clear ice. The graph shows that the minimal thickness for a kid is 4 inches. This figure is unsafe for an adult as it may break the ice. The minimum thickness increases as the weight of the items goes up. Therefore, for a snowmobile the value is 7 inches, for a small car it is between 8 to 12 inches and for a large car, the value is between 12 and 15 inches. In conclusion, this graph gives usefull information and remind people that ice is never 100% safe.

The given graph provides information about coffee and tea manufacturing sales in the year 2018, specifically focusing on the months from August to December.

According to the graph, the sales value for coffee and tea manufacturing was recorded at 30,000 units in August. However, in the subsequent month, September, the value increased to 33,000 units, indicating higher sales during that period.

Furthermore, the graph highlights that the highest sales value occurred in November, reaching 36,000 units. On the other hand, the lowest value can be observed in September, with sales amounting to 21,000 units.

In conclusion, based on the data presented in the graph, it is evident that coffee and tea manufacturing is an important industry for British Columbia.

The given graph provides information on payroll and superannuation in recent years, focusing on countries such as Australia, Austria, and Denmark. Examining the data for Australia, we observe that the value stands at approximately 16.6 percent. Similarly, the graph indicates that Austria also has the same percentage, around 16.6 percent.

In contrast, Denmark has the lowest value among the countries represented in the graph, with a rate of 8 percent. This suggests that Denmark has the smallest proportion of payroll and superannuation compared to Australia and Austria.

In conclusion, both Australia and Austria have the highest percentages of payroll and superannuation among the countries mentioned, with the value being approximately 16.6 percent for each. Meanwhile, Denmark has the lowest percentage at 8 percent.

The given graph provides information about the average costs of running coffee shops, specifically focusing on marketing, administration, food and supply expenses.

According to the graph, the value for lease and utilities is around 10% to 12%. On the other hand, food and supply costs range from 22% to 30%, indicating that this category has a higher percentage of expenses compared to lease and utilities.

Furthermore, the graph highlights that the highest value is for labor costs, ranging from 28% to 35%. This indicates that labor expenses represent a significant portion of the total costs involved in running a coffee shop. Conversely, the lowest value is 5%, which represents miscellaneous expenses.

In conclusion, based on the information presented in the graph, it can be inferred that running a coffee shop is a challenging task.

The given graph provides information about desired effects, specifically focusing on anti-seizure, pain-relieving, and sleep-inducing effects.

According to the graph, THC has the most desired effects on anti-anxiety with 26% while CBD has the most effect on pain relieving with 63%. Furthermore, the graph indicates that CBD has more effects on all the conditions than THC. Conversely, the lowest value is for the anti-seizure effect by THC, which is 10 percent, implying a relatively lower impact on seizure reduction.

In conclusion, based on the information presented in the graph, it can be inferred that CBD has more desired effects compared to THC. CBD exhibits a higher value for anxiety-reducing and pain-relieving effects, indicating its potential for addressing these conditions effectively.

The given graph provides information about COVID-19 cases per 100,000 people as of April 2020 in the 10 densest states in the US.

The graph highlights that the highest value is for New York, with 2,000 cases per 400. This suggests that New York has the highest number of COVID-19 cases among the states included in the graph. On the contrary, Florida has the lowest value, with less than 300 cases per 400, indicating a relatively lower number of COVID-19 cases compared to other states.

In conclusion, based on the information presented in the graph, it is evident that COVID-19 is widespread in the United States. The varying values of cases across different states reflect the varying impact and prevalence of the virus in different regions of the country.

The given graph provides information about the average startup costs for coffee shops, specifically focusing on large shops, café-style setups, and food trucks.

According to the graph, the value for drive-thru coffee shops ranges from $60,000 to $180,000. On the other hand, café-style setups have a higher cost range, from $150,000 to $400,000, indicating that starting a café-style coffee shop is relatively more expensive than a drive-thru.

Furthermore, the graph highlights that the highest value is for large shops, exceeding $750,000. This suggests that starting a large coffee shop incurs significantly higher costs compared to the other categories. Conversely, the lowest value is for kiosks and carts, ranging from $7,000 to $60,000, indicating a relatively lower startup cost for these smaller setups.
